title: Data
text:
This site analyzes monthly street-animal feeding (hayvan besleme) records from the Ankara Provincial Health Directorate (Turkish: Ankara İl Sağlık Müdürlüğü, Sağlık Dairesi). Each row is one neighborhood-day of operations across Ankara’s districts (ilçeler).
We combined eleven monthly Excel workbooks spanning July 2024 through June 2025 into a single tidy dataset:

2024: July, September, October, November, December
2025: January, February, March, April, May, June

Why we chose it: real, public operational data; Turkey-relevant; large enough for time-series and cross-district EDA; and it touches urban policy and animal welfare logistics — a topic with current public-discourse relevance.
Objectives (data-focused):

Publish a reproducible pipeline from many raw .xlsx files to a single tidy object feeding.
Make the cleaned dataset publicly available as feeding_clean.RData.
Document data-quality issues (mixed date formats, text-encoded numbers, coded missing values, typos, source outliers).

We combined eleven monthly Excel workbooks spanning July 2024 through June 2025 into a single tidy dataset:

2024: July, September, October, November, December
2025: January, February, March, April, May, June

Why we chose it: real, public operational data; Turkey-relevant; large enough for time-series and cross-district EDA; and it touches urban policy and animal welfare logistics — a topic with current public-discourse relevance.
Objectives (data-focused):

Publish a reproducible pipeline from many raw .xlsx files to a single tidy object feeding.
Make the cleaned dataset publicly available as feeding_clean.RData.
Document data-quality issues (mixed date formats, text-encoded numbers, coded missing values, typos, source outliers).

title: Data
text:
Accomplishments

Combined 11 monthly workbooks (≈ 3,700+ neighborhood-day rows) into one tibble feeding.
Standardized district / neighborhood labels (trimmed stray spaces such as "GÖLBAŞI ").
Parsed mixed date formats — column 1 is read as a native Excel date where possible; when that is missing (e.g. March 2025 string cells like "1.03.2025"), we fill from the text column with parse_date_from_text() (Excel serials, lubridate, explicit formats).
Parsed text-encoded dry-food amounts into numeric mama_kg (e.g. "84 KG" → 84).
Normalized vehicle / personnel fields: Y3 → 3, - → missing, blank → missing.
Added derived columns yil, ay, yil_ay so the analysis page can compare across months.
Kept a source_file column for traceability back to each monthly workbook.

title: Data
text:
Source and citation
The raw files are monthly publications from Ankara Büyükşehir Belediyesi Sağlık Dairesi (“Sağlık Dairesi Hayvan Besleme Verileri”). Replace this sentence on the deployed site with the exact open-data portal URL + access date before the final submission.

title: Data
text:
Download cleaned data (course requirement)
After Rscript R/prepare_data.R and quarto render, the cleaned dataset is copied to the website:
feeding_clean.RData — R object: feeding (one row per neighborhood-day).

title: Data
text:
Import and preparation
Raw files location in this repository: data/raw/hayvan_besleme_YYYY_MM.xlsx (one workbook per month).
Pipeline (mirrors R/prepare_data.R):

Auto-discover every file under data/raw/ matching hayvan_besleme_*.xlsx.
Read each workbook twice for column 1: native Excel date (covers most months) plus a parallel text pass so we can recover string-encoded dates (e.g. March 2025’s "1.03.2025") and numeric Excel serials if a sheet is ever exported as plain numbers.
Merge the two passes: use as.Date() on the date column; where it is still NA, fill from the text column via parse_date_from_text().
Rename the seven source columns to ASCII snake_case: tarih, ilce, mahalle_sokak, besleme_noktasi_sayisi, mama_kg (via mama_text), arac_sayisi, personel_sayisi, plus metadata source_file.
Trim extra spaces in ilce and mahalle_sokak.
Parse food mass with readr::parse_number() (Turkish decimal comma) from the mama text field.
Parse vehicles: "-" → NA; "Y3" (typo) → 3; otherwise numeric.
Parse personnel: "-" → NA; otherwise numeric.
Combine with purrr::map_dfr(), drop rows whose date failed to parse, add yil / ay / yil_ay, and save feeding to data/feeding_clean.RData.



Code
# Run from the project root once when raw files change:
# Rscript R/prepare_data.R

title: Data
text:
Known data-quality notes

October 2024 workbook contains one row dated 2022-10-18 (clearly a source typo). It is kept in feeding; tag/filter it before yearly aggregations if needed.
March 2025 dates are stored as Turkish DMY strings.
Vehicle / personnel columns are low-variance and frequently use "-" for missing — interpret cautiously.

title: Data
text:
AI use disclosure
If you extend any wording on this page with an AI assistant, mark that paragraph and add a footnote with the prompt (course ethics rule). Verify every quantitative statement against the feeding object.

title: Analysis
text:
Topic: Street-animal feeding operations across Ankara districts (ilçeler) from July 2024 to June 2025, based on monthly health-directorate operational records.
Data: ~3,700+ neighborhood-day records aggregated from 11 monthly workbooks, with feeding-point counts, kg/day of dry food, and vehicle / personnel staffing.
Important aspects: District names needed trimming; food / dates / staff fields were text-encoded with inconsistent formats (March 2025 dates as "1.03.2025", vehicles as "-" or the typo "Y3").
Interesting results: A handful of districts (notably Çankaya, Keçiören, Mamak) dominate row counts; monthly totals fluctuate, and the kg-per-record distribution is right-skewed with consolidated large drops in the tail.
Main outcome: A reproducible Quarto + R pipeline plus a publicly downloadable cleaned .RData enabling year-scale district comparisons and discussion of resource concentration and data quality in municipal animal-welfare operations.

title: Analysis
text:
Monthly volume
How many records per month, and how much dry food (kg) was reported per month?


Code
monthly <- feeding_ts |>
  filter(!is.na(tarih)) |>
  mutate(month_start = lubridate::floor_date(tarih, "month")) |>
  group_by(month_start) |>
  summarise(
    rows = n(),
    total_kg = sum(mama_kg, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(month_start)

p1 <- ggplot(monthly, aes(month_start, rows)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2E86AB") +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b %Y", date_breaks = "1 month") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Records per month") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))

p2 <- ggplot(monthly, aes(month_start, total_kg)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#A23B72") +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b %Y", date_breaks = "1 month") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = " kg", big.mark = ",")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Reported dry food (kg / month)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 35, hjust = 1))

title: Analysis
section: Staff vs food: is the resource allocation linear?
text:
Staff vs food: is the resource allocation linear?

In a perfect world, districts that move more food should have proportionally more staff. Any deviation is either over- or under-staffing.



Code
ops |>
  ggplot(aes(x = median_staff, y = total_kg, label = ilce)) +
  geom_point(color = "#C73E1D", size = 2.5, alpha = 0.85) +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(size = 3, max.overlaps = 30) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_number(suffix = " kg", big.mark = ",")) +
  labs(x = "Median reported staff (per record)",
       y = "Annual total kg of dry food") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)








Figure 10: Median reported staff vs. annual total kg, by district. A flat line indicates uniform staffing across districts.





In this dataset the x-axis collapses to a single value, so the “linear-correlation” question is structurally unanswerable from the source as published — a finding in itself: the municipality is not publishing varying daily staff/vehicle counts.

title: Analysis
section: Weekday vs. weekend, and within-district consistency
text:
Weekday vs. weekend, and within-district consistency

Temporal question: does the operation scale down on weekends, and how stable is each district’s daily load?



Code
wday_lbl <- c("Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun")

by_wday <- feeding_ts |>
  filter(!is.na(tarih), !is.na(mama_kg)) |>
  mutate(wd_int = lubridate::wday(tarih, week_start = 1)) |>
  group_by(wd_int) |>
  summarise(
    rows      = n(),
    median_kg = median(mama_kg, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(wd = factor(wday_lbl[wd_int], levels = wday_lbl))

title: Analysis
text:
Conclusions

Spatial concentration: A handful of districts (Çankaya, Keçiören, Mamak and a few others) account for most of the reported activity. Tying this to population, urban form, or program emphasis remains a hypothesis without external data.
Temporal patterns: Monthly volume is uneven, partly driven by reporting effort rather than real demand. The kg totals are less sensitive to that and offer a more reliable workload proxy.
Right-skewed food amounts: A long upper tail represents consolidated bulk feedings at specific points; the median is a better summary than the mean.
Productivity (kg per resource): With the published staff/vehicle figures fixed at a single value, the ranking of kg-per-staff and kg-per-vehicle reduces to a rescaled total-kg ranking. That itself is a finding — the source does not publish variable daily staffing, so cross-district efficiency comparisons must wait on richer data.
Loading per feeding point: A clear right-skew in kg / feeding point identifies “hot stations” where a single point absorbs disproportionate load — candidates for splitting or route rebalancing.
Staff–food relationship: Because reported personel_sayisi is uniform across districts, the staff-vs-kg scatter collapses to a vertical line; the implied “perfectly linear allocation” assumption cannot be validated from the published file.
Weekday rhythm: Records and median kg per record are visibly lower on weekends in the weekday charts, suggesting the operation does scale down rather than running flat 7 days a week.
Within-district consistency: Coefficient-of-variation across the major districts ranges widely; the highest-CV districts use sporadic bulk drops, while low-CV districts run a flat routine.
Data quality matters: Different months use different date formats, and one row carries an obvious 2022 typo — a reminder that reproducible cleaning is part of the analysis, not a side concern.

title: Street animal feeding in Greater Ankara (Jul 2024 – Jun 2025)
text:
Project summary
This project analyzes a year of street-animal feeding activity (July 2024 – June 2025) published monthly by the Ankara Provincial Health Directorate (Ankara İl Sağlık Müdürlüğü). For each neighborhood-day across Ankara’s districts, the source records how many feeding points operated, the average daily dry food distributed (kg), and the vehicle and personnel staffing used.
We combine eleven monthly workbooks into one tidy dataset to enable district-level and time-series comparisons.
Objectives: (1) describe spatial and temporal patterns; (2) compare districts in terms of feeding intensity; (3) highlight data-quality issues (mixed date formats, coded missings, typos) for transparent reporting.

title: Street animal feeding in Greater Ankara (Jul 2024 – Jun 2025)
text:
Key takeaways

Topic: Municipal street-animal (“sokak hayvanı”) feeding logistics in Greater Ankara over a full year (Jul 2024 – Jun 2025), from official health-directorate operational records.
Data: ~3,700+ neighborhood-day rows aggregated from 11 monthly Excel workbooks, with ilçe, mahalle/sokak, feeding-point counts, kg/day of dry food, and vehicle / personnel staffing.
Important aspects: Mixed date formats across months (some Excel-typed, some Turkish DMY strings like "1.03.2025"); food amounts as "84 KG"; vehicle field includes "-" (missing) and one typo Y3 → 3.
Interesting results: A few districts (Çankaya, Keçiören, Mamak) dominate reported activity; monthly kg totals fluctuate clearly across the year; the kg-per-record distribution has a long right tail (consolidated bulk feedings).
Main outcome: A reproducible Quarto + R pipeline plus a publicly downloadable feeding_clean.RData, ready for the GitHub Pages presentation and HADI PDF submission.
